messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE battle (
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    date TEXT,
    bulgarian_commander TEXT,
    latin_commander TEXT,
    result TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE ship (
    lost_in_battle INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    name TEXT,
    tonnage TEXT,
    ship_type TEXT,
    location TEXT,
    disposition_of_ship TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (lost_in_battle) REFERENCES battle(id)
);

CREATE TABLE death (
    caused_by_ship_id INT,
    id INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    note TEXT,
    killed INT,
    injured INT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (caused_by_ship_id) REFERENCES ship(id)
);

If you just want a list of the battles recorded in the database:

```sql
SELECT
  id,
  name,
  date,
  bulgarian_commander,
  latin_commander,
  result
FROM battle
ORDER BY date, name;
```

If you mean something else by “historical battles” (e.g., only battles where ships were lost, or battles with casualties), tell me which and I’ll tailor the query.
look for battles where more than 10 people got killed

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date;
```
also, the total deaths should be considered across all participants, not just one side

The query I gave already totals deaths across **all participants recorded** (it sums `death.killed` for all `death` rows tied to any ship lost in that battle), not by side.

If you want to be explicit and include battles even when some `killed` values are NULL, use this:

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  b.date,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name, b.date
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.date;
```

If you also store deaths not associated with a specific ship somewhere else, tell me where, and I’ll incorporate those too.
also, I need the names of the battles along with their IDs

```sql
SELECT
  b.id,
  b.name,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.id;
```
make sure to get those unique identifiers for the battles too

`battle.id` is the unique identifier (it’s the PRIMARY KEY). This query returns it along with the battle name and total killed:

```sql
SELECT
  b.id AS battle_id,
  b.name AS battle_name,
  SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) AS total_killed
FROM battle b
LEFT JOIN ship s
  ON s.lost_in_battle = b.id
LEFT JOIN death d
  ON d.caused_by_ship_id = s.id
GROUP BY b.id, b.name
HAVING SUM(COALESCE(d.killed, 0)) > 10
ORDER BY total_killed DESC, b.id;
```
